transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brings me in today is that... for the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always on the go. I'm constantly puttering around the house, fixing things, arranging this and that, or volunteering for just one more thing. It's just... even at 87, I have a really hard time just sitting down and being still.
Do you find that your mood is often elevated or that you feel unusually energetic when you’re doing all these activities?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't feel unusually happy or, you know, on top of the world or anything like that. It's not really a burst of great energy. It's more just... well, I just can't seem to settle down. I feel like I need to be doing something, but my mood itself is just normal.
Do you ever find that your thoughts are racing so much that it's hard to keep up, or do you feel like your mind is jumping from one idea to another very quickly?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My mind is pretty steady, actually. It's not that my thoughts are racing or jumping all over the place... it's really just my body that wants to keep moving. My thinking is perfectly fine, I just can't seem to sit still.
Do you ever feel worried, anxious, or tense when you're not actively doing something?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really an anxious person. It's not that I'm puttering around because I'm worried or nervous about something... I just, well, I just feel like I should be up doing things. If I sit down in my chair to rest, I don't feel tense in my mind, I just feel the urge to get right back up again.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay on task, even when you're trying to do something that needs attention, like reading or following a conversation?

No, I don't really have trouble with that. I can read the paper just fine, and I follow conversations without any problem. It's not my focus that's the issue... I can pay attention to whatever I need to. It's just that while I'm paying attention, my hands or my feet want to be moving. But my concentration is perfectly fine.
Do you ever feel an inner restlessness or a need to keep moving, even when there’s no particular task that needs doing or when you’re by yourself?

Yes, that's exactly it. I do get that feeling. Like, when I'm at the senior center meetings, or... or sitting through the announcements at church, I get this ants-in-my-chair feeling. I just have to shift around in my seat. Sometimes I'll stand up to go get a cup of coffee, or I'll just sit there and straighten my papers just to get through it. There's no real reason for me to be doing those things, I just have that urge to keep moving.
Do you ever find yourself forgetting things more often, or having trouble staying organized with your daily tasks?

No, my memory is sharp as a tack. I don't forget things, and I don't have any trouble keeping my days organized. I keep my calendar, I know when my appointments are, and I get my errands done. It's really just the fidgeting and the needing to move around that I'm dealing with. My mind and my memory are perfectly fine.
Do you feel this same need to move or restlessness in other situations, like during meals, family gatherings, or even just waiting here in the doctor’s office?

Yes, I'd say so. It happens during meals, too. If we're sitting around the table for a long time, especially after everyone's finished eating and they're just talking, I get that same urge. I'll start clearing plates or wiping down the table, just to have an excuse to get up. And even sitting out in the waiting room today, I found myself tapping my foot and flipping through the same magazine twice just to do something with my hands. It's just hard to sit completely still for very long, no matter where I am.
When did you first start feeling this need to keep moving or feeling restless? Was this something you noticed even when you were younger, like as a child or teenager?

Oh, it's been with me my whole life. Yes, even as a young child. I remember... well, back in grade school, I was always getting scolded for popping out of my seat. I would talk over my classmates, too. The teachers used to tell my parents I was just too lively. So, yes, this was happening long before I was even a teenager. It's really just always been the way I am.
Have these feelings of restlessness or the need to keep moving ever caused you any problems in your life, such as difficulties with work, relationships, or other daily activities?

Well, yes, it does cause some friction here and there. For example, I volunteer over at the senior center, and I've had to apologize to people after our committee meetings because I just can't sit quietly through them. And actually, one of my friends there recently suggested I take a smaller role, maybe just sitting at the sign-up table, because my constant moving around and... well, my manner, I guess, was making things a bit tense for everyone else. So, yes, it does get in the way sometimes.
Looking back, were you already having trouble sitting still or feeling restless before you turned 12 years old?
Yes, like I was just mentioning about grade school. I was definitely under 12 back then. So, yes, the trouble sitting still was absolutely happening before I turned 12.
Looking back even further, were you already showing signs of restlessness or trouble sitting still by the time you were around 7 years old?

I... well, it's hard to remember exactly how old I was for every little thing, being 87 now. But yes, I would say so. Seven is right around second grade, isn't it? And like I said, I was already getting in trouble for popping out of my seat and talking too much back in grade school. So I'm sure it was happening by then.
